docs.summary: Why an identify or decode attempt failed. Every failure path returns one of these rather than throwing, so a caller walking a directory of untrusted files never pays for exception unwinding.
The data matched no known container signature.
The container was recognised but no decoder is registered for it.

A decoder is registered and parsed the header, but pixel decoding for this container is not written yet. Distinct from [`NotSupported`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ApertureError~NotSupported) so callers can tell "Aperture has never heard of this" from "Aperture knows this but cannot decode it yet".
The file is well formed but uses a feature this decoder does not implement, such as an arithmetic coded JPEG or an unhandled TIFF compression scheme.
A header field is structurally invalid, out of range or self contradictory.
A bit depth the format does not allow, or that this decoder rejects for the given colour type.
A colour type or sample layout the format does not define.
Width or height is zero, negative or otherwise unusable.
Pixel or metadata payload is corrupt beyond what the decoder can recover from.
The stream ended before a structure that the header promised was complete.
A CRC, checksum or digest embedded in the file did not match the data it covers.
An entropy or dictionary coded stream could not be unpacked.

The file asks for more than [`DecodeOptions`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.DecodeOptions) permits: too many pixels, frames or bytes. Raised before any large allocation happens, so a decompression bomb costs nothing.
An allocation inside the permitted limits still failed.
The underlying stream or file could not be read.
The container is valid but holds no image, for example an ICO with zero entries.
